standard.title: Applying knowledge to spell accurately
standard.description: apply learnt knowledge to spell accurately and to learn new words
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can apply spelling rules and understand word origins and morphemic patterns (AC9E7LY08). They have not yet focused on applying accumulated morphemic and etymological knowledge to the spelling and learning of complex words, or on knowing how to access and use sources for the spelling of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander language words.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply learnt knowledge of morphemic patterns, unusual letter combinations and language-specific resources to spell complex words accurately and learn new words.

nodes.label: Applying morphemic knowledge to complex words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply knowledge of morphemes — prefixes, suffixes, roots — and unusual letter combinations to spell complex words accurately.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply morphemic knowledge to spell at least three complex words correctly, explaining how morpheme analysis guided the spelling.
nodes.typical_width: Apply knowledge of morphemic patterns, etymology and unusual letter combinations to spell complex words accurately across academic and creative writing; use morphemic analysis as a systematic strategy for approaching unfamiliar words.
wider: Investigate how words from particular language origins (e.g. Latin, Greek, French, Arabic) carry predictable morphemic patterns that can be applied to unfamiliar words
Compare morphemic structures across words from different language families and examine what this reveals about borrowing and language history in English

Limited width — this is a skill with thin variation in contexts at this year band. Extension goes deeper: building awareness of etymological research tools and applying them independently to learn large numbers of new words.

response_modes.reason: Spelling accuracy is fundamentally a consolidation skill — knowing morphemic patterns intellectually does not automatically produce accurate spelling under writing conditions. Repeated application across multiple writing contexts builds automaticity.

success_criteria: Spells complex words correctly in own writing, demonstrating application of morphemic knowledge.
Can explain how morpheme analysis (prefix, root, suffix) supports accurate spelling of at least two complex words.

nodes.label: Spelling Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander language words
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and use appropriate sources (e.g. the AIATSIS Map of Indigenous Australia, local First Nations community resources) to access the correct spelling of Aboriginal language and Torres Strait Islander language words.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one appropriate source for the spelling of Aboriginal language or Torres Strait Islander language words and demonstrate correct spelling of at least two words accessed from that source.
nodes.typical_width: Apply knowledge of appropriate sources — including the AIATSIS Map of Indigenous Australia and local First Nations Australian community guidance — to access and use correct spellings of Aboriginal language and Torres Strait Islander language words in own writing.
wider: Investigate how spelling conventions for Aboriginal language words differ from English spelling conventions and what this requires in terms of resource use and cultural respect

Explore how local First Nations community members are the authoritative source for the correct spelling and pronunciation of their community's language words — and what this means for respectful practice
Examine how the AIATSIS Map of Indigenous Australia records language names as a resource for identifying and respecting Country/Place naming conventions
success_criteria: Identifies at least one appropriate source for the spelling of Aboriginal language or Torres Strait Islander language words.
Uses that source to spell at least two words correctly in own writing.
